references.text: The golden calf that the Israelites made while Moses was on the mountain illustrates the violation of the command against making gods out of gold and silver.
Repeats the prohibition against turning to idols and casting graven images.
Moses reminds the people that they saw no form when the Lord spoke, and warns against making carved images.
A curse is pronounced on anyone who makes a carved or cast idol.
The prophet mocks the worship of idols made of metal and wood.
Criticism of those who use gold and silver to make a god that they worship.
Israel is accused of using silver and gold to make idols.
The prophet condemns the uselessness of carved images covered with gold and silver.
Paul urges the Athenians that the divine being should not be likened to images of gold, silver, or stone shaped by human hands.
Paul describes how people exchanged God's glory for images of created things.
Jeremiah explicitly links 'the work of hands' (idols) to the Lord's wrath, concretizing the consequence of breaking Exodus 20:23.
Verse 23 is a direct elaboration of verse 3, where the prohibition against other gods is expanded to include a ban on making them in silver or gold.
Exodus 34:17 reactivates the command from chapter 20 after the incident with the golden calf and emphasizes the permanence of this specific prohibition.
Leviticus 26:1 expands the prohibition from applying only to metal gods to also include stone pillars and carved images, linking it to the holiness of the land.
Deuteronomy 7:25 completes the command by forbidding the desire for the gold on idols, directly addressing 'gods of silver or gold' from Exodus.
